Create a draft contract for a customer's chosen offer.

HTS uses an external payment gateway to tokenize payment cards as well as process payments and payouts.
When HTS is the Merchant of Record (MOR) for the purchase of the order or remitting any product payout to a customer's credit card, HTS requires a tokenized credit card to be present in the `payments` array in the request below.

<details>
<summary>Expand this section for instructions about testing and Spreedly integration.</summary>

The returned payment method token **MxyYEhDK12CUAA18bJDkAq0ab3y** (from the sample response below) should be passed in the `payment_card` type with a `token` identifier as a part of the `payments` array in the request below.

When using the staging environment, make sure to use one of [Adyen's test credit card numbers](https://docs.adyen.com/development-resources/testing/test-card-numbers).

**Tokenization URL**: `https://core.spreedly.com/v1/payment_methods.json`

- Documentation: [Spreedly API docs](https://developer.spreedly.com/reference/create-payment-method)

**Example Tokenization Request**:

```
curl --request POST --url https://core.spreedly.com/v1/payment_methods.json --header 'content-type: application/json' -u  "login:password" --data '{
	"payment_method": {
		"email": "aaa@bbb.com",
		"credit_card": {
			"number": "4000020000000000",
			"month": "03",

}'
```

put.description: Replace the customer contact info (email, phone number, additional email-only notification recipients, and the primary booker's SMS/push notification preferences) on an existing contract. Send the full contact info; it replaces the stored set. This endpoint never sends notifications — recording SMS/push consent does not trigger delivery, and a request that enables SMS without a phone number is rejected as invalid; verifying the change is the partner's responsibility. The email address is validated the same way as during contract creation; an invalid address returns InvalidEmail. Allowed once the contract is confirmed, including fully-redeemed contracts; rejected for unconfirmed drafts and for voided or concluded contracts, which return InvalidContractStatus.

get.description:
Called by HTS to retrieve the current state of a flight booking from the partner system.

HTS provides the booking references stored on the contract as query parameters. These references
are partner-defined key/value pairs (e.g. record locator, order ID) established during contract creation.

The recommended response includes:
- **Booking status** — the current status of the booking (e.g. confirmed, cancelled, voided, pending, checked_in, no_show). Partners may use their own status values; HTS will accept and translate them.
- **Itinerary** — flight slices with segments (origin, destination, departure/arrival times, carrier, flight number, cabin), fare brand, passengers with per-passenger fare amounts, and ancillaries
- **Currency** — ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary amounts
- **Booking references** — the same key/value pairs used to identify the booking
- **Void eligibility** — whether the booking can still be voided (allowed, not_allowed, or allowed_until with an ISO 8601 timestamp)
- **Payment transactions** — amounts, timestamps, transaction types (credit/debit), and payment methods
- **Created at** — ISO 8601 timestamp of when the booking was originally created

Partner implementations may vary in structure and fields returned. HTS is designed to handle
these variations gracefully.

priced.description: Type of offer requested; priced or not. A priced offer can be used to create an order, but has lower rate limits and adds a bit of latency. This should be aligned with the booking flow of the partner: if the offer is made on itineraries that are repriced later in the flow then it’s best to keep it as false here and then call the Price Offers endpoint later in the flow. But if the itinerary is already after the price quote step on the partner side and it might be the final prices we get then setting this option to true returns offers that are priced and can therefore be used as is in the Create Order endpoint, without having to call the Price Offers endpoint. It’s an optimization to facilitate the integration on the partner side. Default: false.

billing_jurisdiction.description: Billing jurisdiction of the user buying the product(s). Recommended for accurate tax calculations at the price offer step, especially if HTS is merchant of record, to avoid corrections at the create order step since it would be after the user has clicked 'book'. This information is usually not known at this step of the flow, but if the offers are created deep in the funnel it might be available, and if setting priced=true to be able to use the offers in the create order endpoint, then it’s important to use this information here to have accurate pricing. Otherwise it’s optional and the price taxes are approximated based on point_of_sale.

partner_supplied.title: partner_supplied
partner_supplied.description: The partner pushes its own rebook inventory. HTS skips fetching inventory and runs the supplied itineraries through the same eligibility, filtering, and ranking as the HTS-sourced flow. Gated per tenant: senders that are not allowlisted receive 422 partner_inventory_not_enabled.

raw_itineraries.description: The partner-supplied itineraries to shop, in the same canonical shape HTS returns from this endpoint. The partner assigns each itinerary a unique id; that id is echoed back in the shop response and is the itinerary_id the partner sends when creating a flight price quote. Each itinerary must end at the final destination of the slice whose segment is disrupted: HTS rebooks through to the slice's final destination rather than replacing only the disrupted segment. For example, for an original slice A->B->C->D where the disrupted segment is B->C, rebook itineraries run from B to D, not B to C. Itineraries that do not end at the slice's final destination are rejected with 400 Bad Request. An empty list yields 204 No Content, the same as an empty HTS shop result. Each itinerary must carry a fare_price (amount and currency); HTS uses it to apply the rebook-allowance filter and to record the redemption amount.

reason.description: Human-readable explanation for why this exercise was performed.

message.description: A human-readable message describing the error
A human-readable message describing the error

refund_method.title: refund_method
refund_method.description: The method by which the refund will be processed.

refundable_payment.title: refundable_payment
refundable_payment.description: The payment details for this payout.

type.description: The partner does not charge the user directly and thus does not have payment information.

search_criteria.title: search_criteria
search_criteria.description: The canonical search HTS applies before shopping one slice of a rebook: the origin/destination airports (original plus nearby) and the departure date window. Partners running their own supplier search must apply these criteria so their rebook options match the HTS-sourced flow. HTS still re-filters and re-ranks whatever is shopped.

slice_index.description: Zero-based position in slices of the slice these criteria search for.

origin_airports.description: Origin airports to search: the original airport plus any nearby airports HTS would include.

destination_airports.description: Destination airports to search: the original airport plus any nearby airports HTS would include.

id.description: Stable identifier for this segment within the contract's rebook eligibility. Echo it back as segment_id on the flight shop request to rebook this exact segment. Stable across eligibility calls for the same disruption.

origin_airport.description: IATA code of the origin airport.

destination_airport.description: IATA code of the destination airport.

departure_date_time.description: Scheduled local departure date and time in ISO Local Date Time format.

arrival_date_time.description: Scheduled local arrival date and time in ISO Local Date Time format.

reservation_booking_designator.description: Reservation Booking Designator (RBD) for this segment: the booking code the airline sold the seat under, one uppercase letter and an optional second letter or digit. Also known as booking class, booking code, class of service, or fare class (e.g. `Y`, `B`, `M`, `Q`, `N`, `J`, `F`, `E1`). Pass the code exactly as it appears on the ticket/PNR.

message.description: A human-readable message describing the error
A human-readable message describing the error
A human-readable message describing the error

shopped_fare_price.title: shopped_fare_price
shopped_fare_price.description: Total price of the fare for this itinerary. Required on each partner-supplied raw itinerary: HTS uses it to apply the rebook-allowance filter and to record the redemption amount. Never present on itineraries in the shop response.

amount.description: Total fare amount, including taxes. Must be greater than zero.

currency.description: Currency of the fare amount, as an ISO 4217 code.

origin_airport.description: IATA code of the origin airport.

destination_airport.description: IATA code of the destination airport.

departure_date_time.description: Scheduled local departure date and time in ISO Local Date Time format.

arrival_date_time.description: Scheduled local arrival date and time in ISO Local Date Time format.

operating_carrier_code.description: IATA operating carrier code, present when the flight is operated by a different carrier.

operating_flight_number.description: Operating flight number, present when the flight is operated under a different number.

reservation_booking_designator.description: Reservation Booking Designator (RBD) for this segment: the booking code the airline sold the seat under, one uppercase letter and an optional second letter or digit. Also known as booking class, booking code, class of service, or fare class (e.g. `Y`, `B`, `M`, `Q`, `N`, `J`, `F`, `E1`). Pass the code exactly as it appears on the ticket/PNR.

fare_brand.description: Name of the fare brand for this slice, if the source provides one.

segments.description: Segments within this slice, each with fare details.

slice1.title: slice
slice1.description: A single leg of the itinerary, containing one or more segments.

segments.description: The flight segments within this slice.

fare_brand.description: The fare brand for this slice.

segments.description: The ordered list of segments that make up this slice.

origin_airport.description: IATA code of the origin airport.

destination_airport.description: IATA code of the destination airport.

departure_date_time.description: Scheduled local departure date and time in ISO Local Date Time format.

arrival_date_time.description: Scheduled local arrival date and time in ISO Local Date Time format.

reservation_booking_designator.description: Reservation Booking Designator (RBD) for this segment: the booking code the airline sold the seat under, one uppercase letter and an optional second letter or digit. Also known as booking class, booking code, class of service, or fare class (e.g. `Y`, `B`, `M`, `Q`, `N`, `J`, `F`, `E1`). Pass the code exactly as it appears on the ticket/PNR.

operating_carrier_code.description: IATA operating carrier code, if different from marketing carrier.

operating_flight_number.description: Operating flight number, if different from marketing flight number.

status_update.title: status_update
status_update.description: The status update that occurred for the flight.

value.description:
The token representing a credit card or a debit card.
 Used to process refunds to the original form of payment.

transaction_type.title: transaction_type
transaction_type.description: Whether this transaction is a charge or refund.

text.description: Description text for this fare detail.

message.description: A human-readable message describing the error
A human-readable message describing the error

verification_status.title: verification_status
verification_status.description:
The partner's verification status for this agent. An opaque partner assertion: this API does not define
 what a partner must do to assert `verified`. Partners that run no verification programme send `not_supported`.

void_policy.title: void_policy
void_policy.description: The void policy for the slice, describing whether and how long a booking can be voided after purchase. If not specified, the void policy is unknown.

void_policy1.title: void_policy
void_policy1.description: Whether the booking is eligible to be voided.

void_window.title: void_window
void_window.description: Customer wants to exercise while the booking's void window is still active.

white_label.title: white_label
white_label.description: The partner's channel that is interacting with the API.

brand.description: The brand name of the white label partner.

PartnerAuth.description:
This API supports authentication via API Key. Clients should include their API key in every request using the `X-Api-Key` header.

**Example Request**:

```
curl --request GET --url https://api.hopper.com/v1/example --header 'X-Api-Key: <your-api-key>'
```
